title: Field-thread batch & patch playbook — customer reply lanes (Aug 2029)
content:
Context: quick synth of field threads from July–Aug 2029. Goal is to group repetitive asks into small, testable 'lanes' so engineering/product can ship micro-patches in 1–3 sprints. This is intentionally pragmatic — thresholds, sample quotes, and suggested owners included.

Method: pulled ~220 threads from support+AM notes (ticket set: CS-1700..CS-1809), filtered by volume and reproducibility, then clustered into 7 lanes. Added rough effort (T/M/L) and metric hooks to measure impact.

High-level lanes (why these matter):
- API stability spikes when using streaming + function-calls (lane-stream-fc). Frequent timeouts and partial outputs — breaks client-side reconcilers.
- Cost/latency variance on dedicated pools during bursts (lane-dedicated-burst). Customers seeing 2x p50 in burst windows.
- Embeddings drift vs. historical index (lane-embed-regressions). Regression alerts not surfaced clearly.
- Rollout fallout: canary -> full rollout mismatch (lane-rollout-telemetry). Missing traceability to input prompts.
- UX confusion: prompt param naming and defaults (lane-docs-and-ui). Docs/SDK mismatch causing integration bugs.
- Observability gaps: token-level attribution missing for composite requests (lane-token-attrib). Hard for customers to debug cost spikes.
- Access controls edge cases for Private installs (lane-private-acls). One-off issues with KMS rotation playbooks.

Raw counts & signals (approx):
- lane-stream-fc: 46 threads (21% of sample), 14 reproduce steps attached. 9 customers requested "automatic retry" behavior.
- lane-dedicated-burst: 38 threads, 11 had telemetry exports attached; recurring in two regions.
- lane-embed-regressions: 29 threads, many after a model swap; customers flagged semantic drift.
- lane-rollout-telemetry: 26 threads, typically after canary-to-prod transition.
- lane-docs-and-ui: 42 threads (includes quickstart issues and SDK naming mismatch).
- lane-token-attrib: 18 threads, usually from platform team customers.
- lane-private-acls: 21 threads, mostly on-prem customers with HSM integrations.

Representative quotes (redacted):
- "When streaming plus function_call happens, the SDK fires partial events and our state machine ends up half-baked." — fintech-ops
- "After we reserved dedicated capacity, we saw latency jumps during schedule spikes — our autoscaler didn't help." — social-app infra
- "Embeddings quality dropped after model pin swap; search recall tanked by ~12% in our test set." — ecom-search

Proposed micro-patches (quick wins, 1–2 sprints):
- lane-docs-and-ui: rename "prompt_template" -> "template" in SDK v3 docs + deprecation note. Effort: S. Metric: decrease in 'param mismatch' tickets by 60% in 4 weeks. Owner: DevEx (Priya).
- lane-stream-fc: add a client-side example and recommended retry pseudo-code in SDK docs; add a server-side 2s buffer to reduce mid-stream timeouts. Effort: M. Metric: reduction in partial-output incidents in support logs by 40%. Owner: serving-runtime (Miguel).
- lane-token-attrib: expose a token attribution debug endpoint (read-only) in Console for enterprise plans. Effort: M. Metric: number of debug calls and decreased investigational time per ticket. Owner: observability (Jordan).

Medium patches (3–6 weeks):
- lane-dedicated-burst: modify autoscale policy templates and introduce a temporary burst buffer per tenant; run canary on 3 customers. Effort: M. Metric: p50/p95 improvement during synthetic bursts. Owner: platform-engineering.
- lane-rollout-telemetry: annotate trace payloads with rollout-id and model-variant. Effort: M. Metric: fraction of rollback investigations with a linked rollout-id increases from 12% -> 80%. Owner: product-hosted-api.

Longer/strategic (quarterly):
- lane-embed-regressions: build an embedding-regression gate in Optimize — automatic regression detection against baseline prompt sets + alerting. Effort: L. Metric: time-to-detect regressions drops from days to minutes. Owner: optimize/applied-ml.
- lane-private-acls: publish a KMS rotation playbook for Private installs and add automated validation checks. Effort: L. Owner: private-deployments/security.

Risk flags / dependencies:
- Any server-side buffer changes need perf baseline runs; slight risk of increased memory usage. (serving-runtime)
- Token attribution endpoints may reveal sensitive token mapping — legal review needed for enterprise privacy. (security/legal)
- Embedding regression detection requires curated baseline datasets from customers — opt-in consent and storage considerations. (privacy/compliance)

Measurement plan (metric hooks to attach to each lane):
- ticket volume by reason-code (pre/post)
- median time-to-resolution for impacted tickets
- client-side error/event rates (for streaming)
- p50/p95 latency under synthetic bursts
- semantic recall for embedding customers (sample test-set)

Open questions / notes to self:
- Confirm whether SDK param rename will break any internal partner integrations (ask Solutions Eng).
- Decide acceptable default for server-side small buffer (2s vs 500ms).
- For embedding regressions, need to scope a minimal beta with 3 customers willing to supply test prompts.

Next steps (short):
1) Socialize playbook in CS weekly sync (Aug 23) — get signoff on owners and priorities.
2) Create JIRA epics for the three quick wins (CS-1830..CS-1832) and assign tentative owners.
3) Kick off legal review for token-attrib endpoint (target 2 weeks).
4) Run a 1-week perf test for server-side buffering and surface results.

Appendix: quick mapping to current product initiatives:
- Docs/UI work maps to DevEx backlog (low cost).
- Stream+function-call work aligns with serving-runtime latency initiative for Q3.
- Embed regression detection complements Optimize roadmap for model quality gates.

Quick checklist (for whoever picks this up):
- [ ] Add CS-1830..CS-1832 tickets and link here
- [ ] Confirm owners in PD sync
- [ ] Schedule perf run for buffer change
- [ ] Draft quickstart SDK example for streaming+function-calls

Tagline: group repeat asks into lanes, ship focused micro-patches, measure with tight hooks.

Notes: informal — expect iterations. If someone grabs an owner, drop a comment and I'll convert to in_review -> final.
